headline: Seven Hospital Ships Now Serve 7.5 Million Bangladeshis Yearly
meta_description: Runa Khan's Friendship organization expanded from one floating hospital in 2002 to seven ships serving Bangladesh's poorest communities and creating over 200,0…
summary_short: What began as a single floating hospital in 2002 has grown into a seven-ship fleet reaching millions of Bangladeshis annually while generating massive employment.
body:
Runa Khan founded Friendship in 2002 with a single floating hospital, an unconventional solution to reach Bangladesh's most isolated and poorest communities. Two decades later, that vision has transformed into a fleet of seven hospital ships serving 7.5 million people every year.

Beyond medical care, Friendship has become an economic engine for the regions it serves. The organization has helped create over 205,000 jobs, bringing sustainable opportunity to communities that often lack basic access to healthcare and employment. By combining mobile medical services with workforce development, Khan's model demonstrates how humanitarian work can address both immediate health needs and long-term economic challenges.

The growth from one vessel to seven reflects both the scale of need in Bangladesh and the proven effectiveness of bringing healthcare directly to people rather than waiting for them to reach distant hospitals. Each ship extends Friendship's reach deeper into waterways and communities that conventional health infrastructure cannot easily serve.
quick_facts: Friendship founded in 2002 with one floating hospital
Now operates seven hospital ships across Bangladesh
Created over 205,000 jobs in poorest communities
